title: The rook and the bishop
outcomes: Taps every square a rook or bishop can reach, including captures and blocked lines
Predicts whether a line is blocked before moving
Tells which of two pieces can reach a square when nobody names the piece

steps.text: The **rook** moves in straight lines: along a rank (sideways) or a file (up and down), as far as it likes. It cannot jump over pieces. To **capture**, it lands on an enemy piece and takes it off the board. It can never land on a square holding its own piece.

steps.caption: The rook slides until something is in the way. It can take the black pawn on d7, but not go past it.

steps.text: The **bishop** moves in diagonals, as far as it likes, and cannot jump. A bishop stays on one colour of square for the whole game: one bishop travels on light squares, the other on dark squares. Captures work just like the rook's.

steps.caption: Four diagonals, but the white pawn on b2 shortens one of them.

steps.text: Before you move a rook or bishop to a square, ask three questions. Is the square on one of my piece's lines? Is anything standing between? Whose piece, if any, is on the square? Empty or enemy: allowed. Your own piece: not allowed.

steps.title: Same rook, one change
steps.prompt: A black pawn appears on d6. Predict first: can the rook still reach d8?

steps.title: Same bishop, one change
steps.prompt: The pawn on f6 changes colour. Predict first: can the bishop still go to f6?
In the mixed round, which answers were guesses? Rate how sure you were overall. (low / medium / high)
